**Hypothesis discrimination**: The next key distinction is between dimerization mechanisms (M2, M3) and simpler mechanisms (M1, M6). Dimerization models predict a nonlinear dependence on catalyst concentration due to the equilibrium between monomeric (cat) and dimeric (cat2) forms.

**Discriminative experiment design**: A higher catalyst concentration (0.1 M) with fixed substrate (1.0 M) will stress the dimerization equilibrium. If dimerization is important, the turnover frequency will decrease compared to the simple mechanism (M1), which predicts linear dependence on [cat].

**Contrastive prediction**: 
- For M2/M3 (dimerization): Initial rate will show reduced turnover frequency at higher [cat] due to dimer formation (less free cat available for catalysis).
- For M1/M6 (no dimerization): Initial rate will increase linearly with [cat] (rate ∝ [cat] at constant [S]).
</hypothesis>
